title: 2000 Miami Dolphins season
summary:
The partial document covers the 2000 Miami Dolphins season, the franchise's 31st NFL season and first under head coach Dave Wannstedt, who replaced the retired Jimmy Johnson. It opens with an overview noting Dan Marino's retirement and his succession by quarterback Jay Fiedler, along with the team's strong performance: a 11–5 record (their best since 1992), an AFC East title (their first since 1994), a fourth consecutive playoff appearance, a Wild Card overtime victory over the Indianapolis Colts (23–17), and a Divisional round shutout loss to the Oakland Raiders (27–0). The document also notes that, as of the 2025 season, this remains Miami's most recent playoff win.

The bulk of the document consists of detailed week-by-week game summaries of the regular season, covering Weeks 1–12 and 17, with Weeks 13–16 left blank. Notable games described include the season-opening shutout of the Seattle Seahawks, a halftime ceremony retiring Dan Marino's number 13, the infamous "Monday Night Miracle" loss to the New York Jets in which the Jets scored 30 fourth-quarter points, wins over divisional rivals Buffalo and New England, a blowout victory over Detroit, a game against San Diego featuring three interception-throwing Chargers quarterbacks, and a bizarre season finale against the Patriots in which officials recalled both teams to the field to replay the final play, securing the division title.

Additional sections cover the playoffs (with detail on the Wild Card win featuring Lamar Smith's club-record 209-yard rushing performance), team standings, and the seven Dolphins players selected for the Pro Bowl, including Jason Taylor, Zach Thomas, Sam Madison, and Trace Armstrong. The document also includes placeholder sections for offseason, staff, roster, preseason, notes, and external links.
